info.title: Copilot Studio Bot Management API
info.version: 2022-01-15 + botauthoring/v1 + botmanagement/v1|v2 + chatbotmanagement (four coexisting route families; see info.x-versioning)
info.description:
The management and authoring surface behind **Copilot Studio** (formerly Power Virtual Agents): an agent's Application Insights configuration, and the dialogs, intents, variable types, fallback, bot provisioning, content, connectors and extensions the authoring client reads and writes.

**This spec covers more than one deployment, and says which is which per operation.** The Application Insights operations were probed live against the environment's own `PowerVirtualAgents` gateway (`pvaRuntimeHost`), whose host must be looked up from the environment record. Everything else was read out of the Copilot Studio maker portal's JavaScript, where the host is a variable injected into the API client at construction and never appears as a literal. Those routes carry their own `servers` entry, and nothing here claims the two hosts are the same machine -- see `info.x-host-families`.

There is no list endpoint on the gateway surface: enumerate agents through the Dataverse `bots` table to obtain a `botId`. Access to the gateway surface is gated on a per-user Copilot Studio licence -- Power Platform tenant-admin rights alone are refused.

Unofficial and reverse-engineered -- see the [README](https://github.com/AdamCoulterOz/powerplatform-apis/tree/main/copilot) for how it was derived and which parts are verified.

openQuestion.question: Is `botApiHost` the same deployment as `pvaRuntimeHost`?
forSame: Both serve a path family rooted at `/api/botmanagement/`. The gateway answers `/api/botmanagement/2022-01-15/environments/{environmentId}/bots/{botId}/...`; the bundle calls `/api/botmanagement/v1/environments/{environmentId}/bots/{botId}/...` and `/api/botmanagement/v2/environments/{environmentId}/bots`. Same shape, same segment names, one segment different.
Both carry `CCI`-prefixed headers unique to this boundary: the gateway requires `x-cci-tenantid`, and every `botauthoring` call sets a header whose bundle key is `_X-CCI-Routing-BotId`.
forDifferent: The extract's own reading of these clients says they are 'served from a regional host injected into the client', which describes the `powerva.microsoft.com` family rather than a per-environment `powervamg.*` gateway.

The gateway host is per environment and the environment id is also in the path; a regional host would serve many environments. Both patterns put the environment id in the path, so the path shape does not settle it.
openQuestion.resolution: Unresolved, and deliberately left so. The two are modelled as separate `servers` entries. Sending a `botauthoring` request to a resolved `pvaRuntimeHost` is the one-request experiment that would settle it; it was not run, because nothing in this spec was executed.

x-notes.note: **Everything added beyond the two Application Insights operations is read from a shipped client, not observed.** It comes from the copilotstudio maker bundle (`main.cb28c5f0.js`, build 0.0.20260903.1-26.08.30-prod, downloaded 2026-09-05). A bundle contains every route the client *can* call, including branches no session exercised, so the coverage is wider than a capture and the confirmation is weaker. Nothing added here is marked `x-probe-verified`, no request was sent, and no response body is described.

**No response body is described anywhere in the added surface, and that is a data limit rather than an omission.** The extract records `responseFieldsRead: []` for all 57 Copilot Studio records without exception, so there is no evidence of a single response field on any of these routes. Each added `200` says so in its description rather than carrying an invented schema.

**Three verbs were bound here that the extract emitted as `null`, and one was corrected.** The extract binds a method only when it sits at the same call site as the url; these four go through `transformOptions({method: ...})` before `http.fetch`, which its binder does not follow. Bound from the evidence string: `GET /api/botmanagement/v2/content/defaultTemplate`, `DELETE .../viral-signup/clear`, `GET .../api/directline/token`. Corrected: `.../viral-signup/create/status` is recorded as POST, but its evidence reads `transformOptions({method:"GET",headers:{Accept:"application/json"}})` in the same statement chain as the url -- GET is used here, and the disagreement is recorded on the operation. Records whose evidence carries no method literal at all were left out of `paths` entirely and are listed in `info.x-adjacent-routes`.

**`etag` is a query parameter on this boundary, not an `If-Match` header.** Five routes take concurrency tokens that way: `DELETE /intents/{id}`, `DELETE /variabletypes/{id}`, `PUT /intents/updateStatus`, `PUT /intents/upsert`, `PUT /intents/clone`. A client written to the HTTP convention will send `If-Match` and be ignored.

**Two headers are written with a leading underscore, and their wire spelling is not established.** Every `botauthoring/v1` call sets header keys spelled exactly `_X-CCI-Routing-BotId` and `_x-ms-solution-unique-name` in the options literal, then passes the literal through `transformOptions()` before `http.fetch`. `transformOptions` is not in the extract, so whether the underscore survives to the wire cannot be read from this evidence. They are declared here under the bundle's spelling, because that is what is actually evidenced; a caller should expect the un-prefixed forms to be what the service reads, given that the probed gateway surface on this same boundary requires a plain `x-cci-tenantid`.

**Query parameters are all optional here, and that is the honest reading of a generated client rather than a shrug.** The nswag clients raise two distinct errors: `The parameter 'x' must be defined` (the caller must pass it, but passing `null` skips appending it to the URL) and `The parameter 'x' cannot be null` (the caller may omit it entirely). Both end up optional *on the wire*, which is what an OpenAPI `required` describes, so none is marked required. Which of the two forms each parameter takes is stated in its description where it was read.

**The extract lists `Accept` among `requestBodyFields` on a dozen records. It is not a body field.** The binder picked up the `Accept` key from the headers object in the same options literal as the body. Body fields are modelled here only where the evidence shows them being serialised -- `connectorIds`/`skipCache`, `aiModelIds`, `pluginLookupId`, and the `category` property the feedback client validates before sending. Everywhere else the body is declared as an unconstrained object with its shape stated as unknown.

**Two POSTs carry no body at all.** `POST .../bots/{botId}/provisioningStatus` and `POST /api/botauthoring/v1/fallback` are both written as `{method:"POST",headers:{Accept:"application/json"}}` with no `body` key -- POST used as an RPC-style read and an RPC-style add. Neither declares a `requestBody` here.

**The declared `security` scope was established for the gateway operations only.** The Copilot Studio first-party audience `96ff4394-9197-43aa-b393-6a41652e21f8` is what the probed Application Insights operations accept. The bundle routes acquire their token inside `transformOptions()`, which the extract does not contain, so the audience for `botApiHost` and `copilotStudioRegionalHost` is not established -- the document-level `security` should be read as a default that has been confirmed for two operations and assumed for the rest.

**Path parameter names are reproduced as the extract wrote them, inconsistencies included.** `/dialogs/{id}` and `/dialogs/{dialogId}/variables` name the same identifier two ways; `/environments/{environmentId}/bots/{cdsBotId}/auth/...` calls the bot id `cdsBotId` where the botmanagement family calls it `botId`. Normalising them would have made the spec tidier and the evidence less traceable.

Live Power Platform admin centre capture shows Copilot Studio agents as resource-query rows carrying `componentsCounts.knowledgeByType`, `channels[]`, `orchestration`, `authentication`, `isWebSearchEnabledForKnowledge`, `sharedWithViewers` and `sharedWithEditors`. Those are read models served by a different service, and no route in this spec manages them -- no bundle route in the Copilot Studio chunk set reads or writes any of those fields. They are recorded here only so a reader who has seen them in the admin centre knows they were checked against this surface and do not belong to it.

Bundle strings are third-party minified JavaScript and were handled as data. The extract's own note says no string read as an instruction directed at the extractor, and none encountered while writing this spec did either.

servers.description: Per-environment PowerVirtualAgents runtime endpoint.

pvaRuntimeHost.description: The environment's PowerVirtualAgents runtime endpoint host. This is not a regional pattern you can compose from a location name: it is an opaque per-environment gateway hostname assigned by the scale unit the environment landed on, and it must be looked up. Read the environment through BAPI (`GET /providers/Microsoft.BusinessAppPlatform/scopes/admin/environments/{environmentId}?api-version=2023-06-01&$expand=properties`) and take `properties.runtimeEndpoints["microsoft.PowerVirtualAgents"]`, then strip the scheme. Hostnames of the form powervamg.<scale-unit>.gateway.prod.island.powerapps.com that do not correspond to a real scale unit do not resolve in DNS, so guessing fails at the network layer rather than with an HTTP error. Environments in the same scale unit share one host; environments in one tenant routinely span several.

tags.name: Application Insights Configuration
tags.description: The Application Insights telemetry wiring of a single Copilot Studio bot: the destination Application Insights resource, and which classes of conversation data - message activities, topic actions, and the user-entered content inside them - are exported to it. This is the observability configuration a maker sets to make conversations analysable and failures debuggable, and the same settings decide how much end-user text leaves the environment.

tags.name: Dialogs
tags.description: A *dialog* is what the Copilot Studio authoring canvas calls a topic: the node graph that runs when a trigger fires. The `botauthoring/v1` client reads, lists, clones, validates and upserts them, and reads the variables a dialog declares. `systemDialogs` are the built-ins an agent gets without an author writing them.

tags.name: Intents
tags.description: The trigger side of a topic: the phrases and conditions that decide which dialog runs. Separately addressable from the dialog itself, with its own clone, search, list and upsert routes, plus a status route that turns triggering on and off without editing the intent. `systemIntents` are the built-ins.

tags.name: Variable Types
tags.description: Author-defined types that agent variables can take -- the third editable authoring resource alongside dialogs and intents, with the same list/clone/upsert/delete shape.

tags.name: Fallback
tags.description: The single fallback behaviour of an agent: what happens when no intent matches. Modelled as a resource with no id -- one per agent, selected by the routing header rather than by a path segment -- which is why `GET`, `POST` and `DELETE` all address the same bare path.

tags.name: Bots
tags.description: Creating an agent and watching it provision, on the `botmanagement/v2` family, plus the v1 route the client calls `openAIApi`. These are the lifecycle operations the maker portal drives; note that neither this family nor the gateway family offers a bot LIST -- see `info.x-adjacent-routes`.

tags.name: Bot Authentication
tags.description: What an agent's authentication connection is depended upon by. One route, asking whether a named connection on a bot has dependent content, optionally counting released content as well as draft.

tags.name: Bot Content
tags.description: The agent's authored content as a document rather than as individual resources: bot components read and written in bulk, and the default template new agents start from. This is the family that speaks `application/json+yaml` as well as JSON.

tags.name: Connectors
tags.description: Connector definitions an agent can call, and the authoring-time intellisense over them. Both are POSTs that read rather than write -- the connector-id list travels in the body because it is a batch lookup, not a query.

tags.name: Extensions
tags.description: Things an agent can be extended with that are neither dialogs nor connectors: Copilot plugins, and AI Builder models. Both are batch lookups by id, POSTed to a regional host rather than to the client's base URL.

tags.name: Viral Signup
tags.description: The self-service trial provisioning job for an environment -- 'viral' being Microsoft's term for a user-initiated signup that provisions capacity without an admin. A three-route job resource: begin, poll, clear.

tags.name: Direct Line
tags.description: A Direct Line token for talking to the agent's runtime, which is what the authoring canvas's test pane needs. The one route on the `chatbotmanagement` family that is about conversing with an agent rather than authoring one.

tags.name: Feedback
tags.description: Maker feedback from the authoring product, posted to the bot-management service. Included because it is a real route on this host, not because it manages anything.

parameters.name: environmentId
parameters.description: Power Platform environment id, as reported by BAPI - the same id used to look up `pvaRuntimeHost`. The host and this id must agree: the gateway serving one scale unit does not answer for environments on another.

parameters.name: botId
parameters.description: Primary key of the bot's row in the environment's Dataverse `bot` table. This API has no list endpoint, so callers discover bot ids through the Dataverse Web API: `GET https://{dataverseHost}/api/data/v9.2/bots?$select=botid,name`. `bot` is a solution-provisioned custom table (entity set `bots`, primary id `botid`, primary name `name`) that exists only in environments where Copilot Studio has provisioned it; environments that have never had a bot return an empty `value` array rather than an error, and an environment with no Dataverse cannot host bots at all. See the dataverse spec in this repo.

parameters.name: x-cci-tenantid
parameters.description: Entra tenant id of the environment. Mandatory, not derived from the bearer token, and spelled in lower case on the wire.

get.description:
Returns where a Copilot Studio bot ships its conversation telemetry and how much of each conversation is included.

The response carries the Application Insights connection string in clear text. That string is a write credential for the target resource, so this read is not as harmless as its verb suggests.

**Host.** The base URL is the environment's own PowerVirtualAgents gateway, an opaque per-environment hostname that must be read from BAPI's `properties.runtimeEndpoints["microsoft.PowerVirtualAgents"]` rather than composed from a region - see the `pvaRuntimeHost` server variable. The host and the `environmentId` in the path must agree; a gateway answers only for the environments on its own scale unit.

**Tenant header.** `x-cci-tenantid` is mandatory on every call and is not inferred from the bearer token. It is the easiest part of the request to leave out, because nothing about the URL hints that it exists.

**Finding a `botId`.** This API has no list endpoint - the parent `.../bots` collection is not a route. Bots are rows in the environment's Dataverse `bot` table, so callers enumerate them through the Dataverse Web API (`GET https://{dataverseHost}/api/data/v9.2/bots?$select=botid,name`) and use the `botid` primary key here.

**Versioning.** `2022-01-15` is part of the route, not an `api-version` query parameter. An `?api-version=` query string is ignored; a different date in the path is not a route at all.

**Licensing.** Access is gated on the calling *user* holding a Copilot Studio licence. This is a maker surface, not an admin surface: Power Platform tenant-administrator rights do not substitute, and the licence check runs before the tenant header, the environment id and the bot id are examined, so an unlicensed caller cannot tell a bad request from a good one.

Not verified: the 200 response body, which is provider-derived - every request in this tenant stopped at the 403 licence gate.

200.description: The bot's Application Insights configuration.

401.description: No bearer token, or one the service will not accept: `ErrorCode` 1000, `UnauthenticatedUser`. Acquire a token for the Copilot Studio audience and retry; a token for another Power Platform audience will not do.

403.description: Authenticated, but the calling user holds no Copilot Studio licence: `ErrorCode` 4030, `UserHasNoLicense`. Not retryable and not fixable by granting Power Platform admin rights - the user needs the licence. Because this check runs first, a 403 says nothing about whether the bot, the environment or the tenant header were valid.

404.description: Empty body, no error envelope. Returned for any path the gateway does not route: the parent `.../bots` collection, `.../bots/{botId}` on its own, or a different date in the api-version segment. An empty-bodied 404 therefore means the URL is wrong, not that the bot is missing.

put.x-probe-notes: Entirely provider-derived. Never executed: this is a mutation, the only bot in the probe tenant is a real user-owned bot, and creating a throwaway bot to write against was not possible because the same licence gate that blocks the read blocks bot creation. Request shape, accepted statuses and the in-band `errors` semantics come from the provider client and its unit tests.

200.description: The stored configuration - **or** a rejection. Inspect `errors`: non-empty means the update was refused and its text is the reason. Empty means it was applied, and the body is the configuration as stored.

401.description: No bearer token, or one the service will not accept: `ErrorCode` 1000, `UnauthenticatedUser`.

403.description: Authenticated, but the calling user holds no Copilot Studio licence: `ErrorCode` 4030, `UserHasNoLicense`. Not retryable.

500.description: The update was rejected. Terminal, not transient: do not retry, fix the request. Keep this status out of any retry policy and surface the raw body as the error, since it is not guaranteed to be the standard error envelope — treat it as opaque text.

AppInsightsConfiguration.description:
The Application Insights wiring of one Copilot Studio bot: which Application Insights resource its conversation telemetry is shipped to, and how much of each conversation is included in what is shipped.

Export means the bot emits a custom event per logged item as conversations run, so the three inclusion flags govern both the detail available for analysis and the volume - and cost - of ingested data. See https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-copilot-studio/advanced-bot-framework-composer-capture-telemetry.

The update replaces the whole object, so send every member on a write rather than relying on omitted fields keeping their stored value.

environmentId.description: Echoed by the service on both operations, but not necessarily equal to the `environmentId` in the request path - prefer the id you addressed over the one reported back.

botId.description: Echoed by the service; like `environmentId`, prefer the caller's value over the echoed one.

appInsightsConnectionString.description: Where telemetry is sent: an Application Insights connection string in the modern semicolon-delimited `key=value` form, not a bare instrumentation key. It carries the ingestion endpoint as well as the key, so the target resource may live in a different region from the environment. This is the master switch - the empty string stops telemetry export regardless of the inclusion flags below. It is also a credential: anyone holding it can write telemetry into the resource, so treat a read of this configuration as a read of a secret. See https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/azure-monitor/app/connection-strings.

includeActivities.description: Log conversation *activities*: the details of incoming and outgoing messages and events, each becoming a custom event carrying its type, direction, channel and timing. This is the coarse conversational transcript - enough to see that a turn happened and how long it took - and the highest-volume of the three flags. Off means no per-message events at all.

includeActions.description: Log an event each time a node within a topic is executed, so a conversation can be traced through the authoring canvas: which topic was triggered, which branch was taken, where it stopped. This is what makes a failed conversation debuggable at the level of the topic that broke rather than only visible as a bad turn. Independent of `includeActivities`.

includeSensitiveInformation.description: Include the *content* of what is logged rather than only its structure: sensitive properties such as user id, user name and message text. With it off, activity and action events are emitted with those properties stripped, so the telemetry shows shape and timing but not what anyone typed. With it on, end-user text - and any Dataverse values the bot has loaded into variables and echoed into messages - is exported to the Application Insights resource, leaving the environment's compliance boundary for one with its own retention, geography and access control. The flag to think hardest about before setting.

networkIsolation.description:
How the bot reaches the Application Insights ingestion endpoint: over the public internet, or constrained to a private path for a network-isolated environment.

`PublicNetwork` is what an ordinary environment carries, and it is the only value listed here. The accepted set is open and very probably larger - a network-isolated environment must have something else to say - so round-trip whatever a read returned rather than treating this list as closed.

errors.description: In-band failure text on the update. The service reports a rejected configuration here on an otherwise normal 200 response, so a 200 alone does not mean the update was applied - this field must be checked. Empty string when there is nothing to report, and sent as `""` on the way in as well, since the update round-trips the whole object.

ErrorResponse.description: The bot-management error envelope, returned for every failure that reaches the service's own handlers. The flat `ErrorCode`/`ErrorMessage` pair duplicates the nested `Error.Code`/`Error.Message`; the nested object is the richer one. Routes the gateway does not recognise are rejected earlier and return no body at all.

ErrorCode.description: Numeric error code, distinct from the HTTP status. Observed: 1000 alongside 401 (`UnauthenticatedUser`), 4030 alongside 403 (`UserHasNoLicense`). The set is open - only these two were reachable - so it carries no `enum`; prefer `Error.Code`, which is symbolic and self-describing.

ErrorMessage.description: Human-readable text, duplicating `Error.Message`. Terse and not localised in anything observed; suitable for logs, not for end users.

ErrorInfo.description: Legacy sibling of `Error`, superseded by it. Explicitly null in every observed response, so its populated type is unknown and no `type` is asserted.

ErrorDetail.description: The structured half of the error envelope: a symbolic code to branch on, a message to log, and slots for retry guidance, nested causes and diagnostic context that the failures observed here leave empty.

Code.description: Symbolic error code, and the field worth branching on. `UnauthenticatedUser` means no usable bearer token reached the service; `UserHasNoLicense` means the calling user holds no Copilot Studio licence. The set is open - the licence gate answered first and hid every other code - so it carries no `enum`; `x-observed-values` lists what was actually seen.

Message.description: Human-readable text for the code, duplicated into `ErrorMessage`.

RetryIn.description: How long the caller should wait before retrying, populated on throttling responses. Explicitly null on every error observed here, consistent with those errors being permanent rather than transient; because only nulls were seen, its populated type and units are unknown and no `type` is asserted.

InnerErrors.description: Nested causes, when one failure was produced by another. Empty in every observed response, so the element shape is unknown and left open.

Properties.description: Free-form key/value context specific to the error code - the identifier that was rejected, the quota that was exceeded. Empty in every observed response.

Diagnostics.description: Correlation and tracing context for a support case. Explicitly null in every observed response, so no `type` is asserted.

cciRoutingBotId.name: _X-CCI-Routing-BotId
cciRoutingBotId.description:
Which agent the call is about. The `botauthoring/v1` routes carry no bot id in the path -- dialogs, intents, variable types and fallback are all addressed as if there were only one agent, and this header is what selects it. The client sets it on every call, falling back to the empty string when it has no id.

**The leading underscore is what the bundle writes**, verbatim: `"_X-CCI-Routing-BotId"`. The options literal is then passed through `transformOptions()`, which is not in the extract, so whether the underscore reaches the wire is unestablished. Expect the un-prefixed `X-CCI-Routing-BotId` to be the real header name, on the strength of the probed `x-cci-tenantid` on this same boundary.

solutionUniqueName.name: _x-ms-solution-unique-name
solutionUniqueName.description:
Scopes the call to one Dataverse solution, so authoring resources resolve within the solution the maker is working in rather than across the whole environment. Set on every `botauthoring/v1` route except the two that take a bot id in the path, again defaulting to the empty string.

The leading underscore is the bundle's literal spelling; see `_X-CCI-Routing-BotId` for why it may not be the wire name.

csEnvironmentId.name: environmentId
csEnvironmentId.description: Power Platform environment id. On these routes it is a path segment; the tenant id is not present at all, unlike the `chatbotmanagement` family.

csBotId.name: botId
csBotId.description: The agent's id -- the primary key of its row in the environment's Dataverse `bot` table. This API family has no list endpoint; enumerate through the Dataverse Web API (`GET https://{dataverseHost}/api/data/v9.2/bots?$select=botid,name`) or see `info.x-adjacent-routes` for the PowerApps-hosted `listBots` route.

csTenantId.name: tenantId
csTenantId.description: Entra tenant id. The `chatbotmanagement` family is the only one here that puts it in the path; the probed gateway family sends it in the `x-cci-tenantid` header instead.

csCdsBotId.name: cdsBotId
csCdsBotId.description: The agent's id, spelled `cdsBotId` on this route and `botId` on every other -- the extract's spelling is kept rather than normalised. Same Dataverse `bot` primary key.

csConnectionName.name: connectionName
csConnectionName.description: The name of the authentication connection on the agent whose dependencies are being read. A connection name, not a GUID.

csDialogId.name: dialogId
csDialogId.description: The dialog whose variables are read. Spelled `dialogId` here and `id` on `GET /api/botauthoring/v1/dialogs/{id}`; both name the same thing.

csDialogIdShort.name: id
csDialogIdShort.description: The dialog to read. Note that `clone`, `upsert`, `validate`, `systemDialogs` and `actionNodeFromFlow` are sibling literal segments at this position, so a dialog id that collides with one of those words is not addressable here.

csIntentId.name: id
csIntentId.description: The intent to delete. As with dialogs, several sibling segments at this position are literals (`clone`, `search`, `systemIntents`, `updateStatus`, `upsert`, `upsertDetails`, `upsertList`).

csIntellisenseParam.name: param
csIntellisenseParam.description: **Unnamed in the evidence.** The client method takes it as its first positional argument and concatenates it onto `/api/connectorintellisense/`; the minified parameter name carries no meaning and nothing in the surrounding code names the value. It is left as `param` rather than given an invented name.
